name: Perturbative SM: every Yukawa term is a fermion bilinear with zero net B and L

source.located: The result is the accidental-symmetry property of the renormalizable SM: Weinberg, PRL 43 (1979) 1566 ('Baryon- and lepton-nonconserving processes'; not on arXiv); anomaly caveat 't Hooft, PRL 37 (1976) 8 (not on arXiv). Intended arXiv restatements: Brivio & Trott 1706.08945 (SMEFT review) and Rubakov & Shaposhnikov hep-ph/9603208 (the tree's own READ source for the anomaly).

published_statement: NOT QUOTED (source not readable here). What the tree attributes, and what this stage re-derived: in the SM with its standard field content and renormalizable (dimension <= 4) Lagrangian, every gauge-invariant Yukawa term (Qbar H d_R, Qbar H~ u_R, Lbar H e_R) carries B = L = 0, so B and L are accidental global symmetries at the classical/perturbative level; each is violated non-perturbatively by the SU(2) (and U(1)_Y) anomaly, B - L being anomaly-free under the SM gauge fields. Standard attribution (NAMED-NOT-READ): Weinberg 1979 states that the first B- or L-violating operators consistent with SM gauge symmetry are dimension 5 (LLHH, Delta L = 2) and dimension 6 (four-fermion, Delta B = Delta L).
published_hypotheses: SM gauge group SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1)_Y with the standard chiral field content Q, u_R, d_R, L, e_R per generation, one Higgs doublet (as re-derived)
renormalizability: only operators of mass dimension <= 4 (standard, NAMED-NOT-READ in the source; its failure is computed here)
B = 1/3 per quark, L = 1 per lepton, H neutral (assignments, not data)
perturbative / classical level only: the SU(2)^2 and Y^2 anomalies of B and L (computed here: 1/2 and -1/2 per generation each) violate B + L non-perturbatively
no right-handed neutrino in the minimal SM (its addition is computed here to be harmless for the Yukawa claim)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (unnamed): renormalizability / mass dimension <= 4. massform.py:2451 carries C3 as 'THEOREM (perturbative SM)' and massform.py:486-488, :171-172, :719 and :2918 state 'no Higgs coupling carries B or L' with hypotheses 'perturbative SM field content and B, L assignments (_Q table)' + H-BL. Dimension <= 4 is implicit in 'SM' but not named. It matters: the dimension-5 Weinberg operator (eps L H)(eps L H) is gauge-invariant (hypercharge 0, SU(2)-invariant to 2.5e-14 under 200 random SU(2), non-vanishing) and carries Delta L = 2, a Higgs coupling carrying L (rederive (2c),(3)).

WEAKENED-BUT-COVERED: for B (the half every refusal uses), the Higgs-bearing B-carriers first appear at dimension 7 (8 structures psi^4 H, all with Delta B = -Delta L, rederive (2e)); there are none at dim 5 or in psi^2 phi^3 at dim 6; the dim-6 B-violators are four-fermion with no Higgs. All 18 Higgs-bearing B/L carriers at dim 5-7 violate B - L, so the tree's NAMED H-BL (massform.py:832-833) excludes them. At dimension 8, B - L-CONSERVING Higgs-bearing B carriers exist (18 structures, e.g. H H+ L Q Q Q = (H+H) x QQQL, rederive (2g)); only dimension <= 4 excludes those, not H-BL.

GENERALISED, HOLDS: 'every Yukawa term' (massform.py:2049-2053, three terms) -> 'no Higgs coupling' (massform.py:487-488). At dim <= 4 the only other Higgs couplings are |D H|^2 and V(H) (phi^4 enumerated: H H H+ H+), which contain no fermions and carry B = L = 0 trivially. The three listed terms are exactly the complete set of gauge-invariant psi psi phi structures (rederive (2)); flavour indices do not matter since B, L are generation-universal.

UNNAMED BUT HARMLESS: minimal content without nu_R (_Q at massform.py:2047-2048; H-FLAV at :834 assumes massless neutrinos for the flavour sub-count only). Adding nu_R adds the Dirac Yukawa L H nc with B = L = 0 (rederive (2b)); the Majorana bare mass nc nc carries L = -2 but contains no Higgs, so C3 as a Higgs statement survives it (H-BL does not; that is a different key).

RETAINED CORRECTLY: 'perturbative'. B and L each carry SU(2)^2 anomaly 1/2 and Y^2 anomaly -1/2 per generation, equal, so B - L is SM-gauge-anomaly-free and B + L is not (rederive (4)); the tree prices the anomaly route separately (S11, massform.py:512-560). No drift. Recorded, outside this key: grav x (B - L) = -1 per generation without nu_R (rederive (4)), relevant to H-BL, not to C3.

rederivation.outcome: PASS (exit 0; output in rederive/sm-yukawa-bl-charges.out). (1) massform's own _Q and YUKAWA_TERMS, read by AST (no import, nothing written under research/), give B = L = 0 for y_e, y_d, y_u. (2) Exhaustive enumeration of derivative-free Lorentz-scalar gauge-invariant operators from SM Weyl fields + H, H+ (hypercharge 0, SU(3) triality 0, even doublets, even LH and even RH fermion counts; exact rational arithmetic): dim 4 psi psi phi = exactly {Q uc H, Q dc H+, L ec H+} + h.c., all B = L = 0, matching the tree's three terms; no dim-3 bare mass; dim-4 phi^4 only. (2b) +nu_R: Dirac Yukawa B = L = 0; Majorana bare mass L = 2, no Higgs. (2c) dim 5: only L L H H (+h.c.), Delta L = 2. (2d) dim 6: 8 B-violating four-fermion structures, none with a Higgs; no psi^2 phi^3 carrying B or L. (2e) dim 7: 8 Higgs-bearing Delta B != 0 structures, all Delta B = -Delta L; 8 with Delta L = 2, Delta B = 0. (2f) all 18 dim 5-7 Higgs-bearing carriers violate B - L. (2g) dim 8: 18 B - L-conserving Higgs-bearing Delta B = Delta L structures incl. (H+H)QQQL. (3) Weinberg contraction SU(2)-invariant (max deviation 2.5e-14) and non-zero. (4) anomalies per generation: B and L each SU(2)^2 = 1/2, Y^2 = -1/2, SU(3)^2(B) = 0; B - L gauge-anomaly-free; B + L anomalous. Limitation: counting conditions ignore flavour antisymmetry (irrelevant at dim 4, where the list is exact); dim >= 5 counts are structure counts, not independent-operator counts.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The SM's B/L accidental symmetry (1967-1979) was built with neutrinos massless and no Delta B or Delta L observed. Data it lacked: neutrino masses (established by oscillations from 1998). EVIDENCE THAT IT MATTERS: nonzero neutrino mass requires field content or operators beyond the minimal renormalizable SM; one data-allowed completion, the dim-5 Weinberg operator, is a Higgs coupling carrying Delta L = 2 (computed here, gauge-invariant and non-vanishing), so the tree's 'no Higgs coupling carries ... L' is not a theorem about nature but about the renormalizable model. EVIDENCE THAT IT DOES NOT MOVE THE TREE'S CONCLUSION: (a) the other completion, a Dirac nu_R Yukawa, carries B = L = 0 (computed); (b) the refusals C3 carries (DISPLACEMENT, QUANTA, CREATION: 'forms no net baryon number') rest on B, and no Higgs-bearing operator carries B below dimension 7; every one at dims 5-7 violates B - L and is excluded by the tree's named H-BL; (c) no Delta B has ever been observed (proton-lifetime limits, recalled not read). A later datum therefore narrows the L-half and leaves the B-half standing; the one residual B-carrying class not covered by H-BL is dimension >= 8 (e.g. (H+H)QQQL), excluded only by renormalizability. Nothing here shows a computational error in the result or in massform's table.
grade_evidence: Within its stated scope the result is re-derived exactly: the three terms in massform.py:2049-2053 are the complete gauge-invariant psi psi H set and each carries B = L = 0 (rederive (1),(2)); 'perturbative' is correctly kept (B + L anomalous, rederive (4)). The narrowing is a DROPPED HYPOTHESIS, not an error: massform.py:487-488/:171-172/:2918 generalise to 'no Higgs coupling carries B or L' under 'THEOREM (perturbative SM)' (:2451) without naming renormalizability (dimension <= 4). Computed counterexample to the unrestricted L statement: the dim-5 Weinberg operator (eps L H)^2, gauge-invariant and non-zero, Delta L = 2 (rederive (2c),(3)); neutrino masses are measured, so this class is data-allowed. For B the claim holds through dim 6 and, with the tree's named H-BL, through dim 7; at dim 8 B - L-conserving Higgs-bearing B carriers exist (rederive (2g)) and only dim <= 4 excludes them. The conclusion the refusals use (no net B from Higgs couplings) is not moved by any datum. Source not READ this stage (quota/egress), so no published sentence is quoted; the grade rests on the re-derivation. Suggested named hypothesis for the tree (not applied): H-DIM4, 'renormalizable SM couplings only; a dim-5 Weinberg term would carry Delta L = 2 (L-half of C3 fails, B-half unaffected)'.
what_would_change_the_grade: -> STANDS: C3's hypotheses name dimension <= 4 (or the tree restricts the statement to B, with H-BL cited for dims 5-7), or a READ of Weinberg 1979 / a restating review confirming the tree states exactly the source's scope. -> DATA-DEPENDENT for the L-half: if the tree's use came to rest on L (not only B), since Dirac vs Majorana is undetermined. -> WRONG: only an explicit gauge-invariant dimension-4 Higgs coupling with B or L != 0 in the SM field content, which the exhaustive enumeration here excludes. -> OPEN is not warranted: the claim is finite and fully checked here; only the source reading is missing.
